title: Short Stuff: Selling the Brooklyn Bridge
summary: Short Stuff episode on George C. Parker, a con man who sold the Brooklyn Bridge (and other New York landmarks such as the Statue of Liberty, Madison Square Garden, Grant's Tomb, and the Met) to gullible, often newly arrived immigrants around Ellis Island. The hosts cover how the scam worked, why the bridge's old tolls made it believable, the inflation-adjusted value of a sale (about five million dollars), Ellis Island warnings against such purchases, and Parker's eventual downfall under New York's four-strikes "Baumes Law," which led to life in Sing Sing for a bounced check. The hosts also note doubts about some claims, such as a pamphlet's existence and the claim that he sold the bridge multiple times a week.
topics: inflation calculation of five million dollars

segments.title: Introduction to George C. Parker
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode about selling the Brooklyn Bridge and describes George C. Parker as a con man who claimed, probably exaggeratedly, to sell it repeatedly.

segments.title: How the Brooklyn Bridge scam worked
segments.summary: Immigrants arriving at Ellis Island, some with money, were targeted by informants and by Parker, who showed them deeds and sold them the bridge as a toll-earning investment. Tolls on the bridge, which were charged until 1891 for pedestrians and vehicles and for roadway traffic until 1911, made the claim seem plausible.

segments.title: Why the scam worked and other landmarks sold
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the bridge's symbolic status as one of two major American symbols alongside the Statue of Liberty, and that Parker sold other places such as monuments, land, and parks, with sales reportedly reaching as high as fifty thousand dollars.

segments.title: Break and inflation calculation
segments.summary: The hosts take a break and then report that fifty thousand dollars in that era is about five million dollars today.
topics: inflation calculation of five million dollars

segments.title: Ellis Island warnings and doubtful claims
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the spread of the scam, including a disputed William McClowney alias and Ellis Island signage warning immigrants not to buy landmarks, while noting doubts about whether a pamphlet and the claim that public buildings cannot be sold are true. They also mention Parker reportedly sold the Met, Madison Square Garden, and Grant's Tomb.

segments.title: Parker's downfall under the four-strikes law
segments.summary: Parker was convicted under New York's four-felony law, the Baumes Law, after passing a bounced hundred-and-fifty-dollar check, and was sentenced to life at Sing Sing. The hosts joke about baseball's strikes.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the Short Stuff episode and note the show is an iHeartRadio production.
